sections.title: Georgia corporate income and franchise taxes

rows.label: Corporate income tax rate
rows.note: Flat rate on Georgia taxable net income. HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026) cut the rate from 5.19% to 4.99% beginning January 1, 2026, per the Governor's office.

sections.title: Georgia property tax: state rules

rows.label: Levied by
rows.value: County governing authorities, other local taxing jurisdictions and boards of education
rows.note: Each taxing jurisdiction sets its own millage rate every year.

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Filing Property Tax in Georgia

rows.label: State oversight
rows.value: Georgia Department of Revenue, Local Government Services
rows.note: County boards of tax assessors value property; the Revenue Commissioner checks county digests for uniformity.

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Local Government Services

rows.label: Assessment ratio
rows.note: Property is taxed on 40% of fair market value unless the law says otherwise (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Property Tax Valuation

rows.label: Statewide standard homestead exemption
rows.note: Deducted from the 40% assessed value; applies to county and school taxes. Many counties grant larger local exemptions.

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Property Tax Homestead Exemptions
Georgia Department of Revenue: Filing Property Tax in Georgia

sections.title: Georgia real estate transfer tax

rows.label: Real estate transfer tax rate
rows.value: $1.00 for the first $1,000 of sale price plus $0.10 per additional $100 (about $1.00 per $1,000)
rows.note: Paid before the deed can be recorded with the clerk of the superior court (O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 to 48-6-10).

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Real Estate Transfer Tax

rows.label: Who pays the transfer tax
rows.value: Seller (by law); the contract may shift it to the buyer

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Real Estate Transfer Tax

rows.label: Intangible recording tax on long-term mortgage notes
rows.value: $1.50 per $500 of the note's face amount (maximum $25,000 per note)
rows.note: Charged when the security instrument for a long-term note secured by Georgia real estate is recorded; the lender may pass it on to the borrower.

source.title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Intangible Recording Tax
